opulent

/OP-yuh-luhnt/ - the stress falls on OP · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Opulent means characterized by rich abundance verging on ostentation.

The wedding tent was opulent beyond anything the invitation hinted: silk carpets over the grass, towers of peonies, and waiters pouring from gold pitchers.

Worked Example

The sultan's guest suite stopped conversation: carpets six layers deep, perfumed fountains, pomegranates stacked in silver towers — an opulent display meant to say the household had wealth to waste.

Opulent goes beyond 'luxurious' — luxury can be quiet, but opulence performs: the abundance is arranged to be seen, rich to the point of showing off.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sumptuous: Sumptuous means rich and costly in the materials themselves — velvet, marble, aged silk — luxury you can touch and taste. Opulent adds performance: the abundance is arranged to be noticed, wealth staged for an audience. Sumptuous needs no spectators at all; opulent exists to be seen.

lavish: Lavish praises the spending — a lavish party, lavish gifts — generosity poured out without counting the cost. Opulent describes the resulting look: massed wealth on display, rooms and feasts performing their riches. A host is lavish in what they pour out; the ballroom they fill is opulent.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

spartan: stripped to the bare essentials on purpose

plain: without decoration of any kind

Where it sits · how loudly wealth is displayed — comfortable → plush → opulent

comfortable vs. opulent: Comfortable stops short of opulent — comfort asks only that nothing pinch; it makes no show of wealth at all.

plush vs. opulent: Plush stops short of opulent — a plush seat pampers you quietly, while an opulent room performs its riches for everyone in it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — op

Root — op: wealth, resources (Latin ops)

Suffix — -ulent

Suffix — -ulent: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Op- (Latin ops, 'wealth, resources') + -ulent ('full of') = full of wealth. Rome even had a harvest goddess named Ops, plenty personified; an opulent room is stuffed with her gifts — and makes sure you notice.

Use the root in a new word: copious

Use the root in a new word: copious: You met copious earlier in this course — co- ('together') plus the same ops root: resources heaped up, as in copious notes.

Word Choice

formal / admiring or arch

Opulent can flatter or needle, and this unit's neighbors mark its edges: lavish (in the reference list) praises generous spending, while opulent describes the look of massed wealth — and can hint at showing off. If the riches tip into tastelessness outright, English reaches past opulent to gaudy.
